transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump says he stands by Defense Secretary Pete Hacksath,
who could face an impeachment vote in the House this week.
He won the war in two places, two big places,
very important, very impactful, and they were won.
Not like Vietnam, where nothing was won, or Afghanistan, or Iraq,
or any of these wars, where nothing was won.
There was nothing won, just lots of death, and then let's leave.
In one case, they're not going to have a nuclear weapon.
In the other, we're making hundreds of billions of dollars for this country.
Speaking to reporters, Trump pointed to Venezuela and Iran.
Hacksath says he will hold a press conference later this morning
to address the impeachment resolution filed by outgoing Kentucky Republican Congressman Thomas Massey.
Massey filed it Monday as a House open backup
following the midterm elections at press conference.
He will be Hacksath's first at the Pentagon in six months.
Saudi Arabia's key oil pipeline that bypasses Iran's chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz has been struck.
In Peirziah Betroury reports this is the second time the pipeline has been hit
following drone attacks on its pumping stations in September.
The east-west pipeline runs cross-country
and carries millions of barrels of crude a day
from Saudi Arabia's oil-rich eastern coast to its western ports in the Red Sea.
The kingdom's been able to use the roughly 750-mile long pipeline
to export oil through a much longer route than the one running through the Strait of Hormuz.
But the Saudi Energy Ministry says the pipeline was targeted on Monday, causing a fire.
It did not offer further details on the nature of the attack.
Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, however, have been attacking Saudi energy sites with missiles and drones.
The group hit Saudi oil company Aramco's skyscraper in the capital of Riyadh just this weekend.
The Houthis say Saudi airstrikes have killed scores of people in Yemen.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
The man accused of killing conservative activist Charlie Kirk on a Utah college campus now has a trial date.
Hugo Rickard Bell of Member Station KUER reports.
June 21, 2028. That's when jury selection will begin in Tyler Robinson's trial.
Fourth District Judge Tony Graf ruled.
This trial setting and case management order's intent is to ensure that the constitutional rights
of Mr. Robinson and Mrs. Kirk are upheld at every junction.
Kirk's widow Erica requested a speedy trial several times.
In court, her attorney Jeffrey Nyman told Judge Graf that the trial date he set was not appropriate.
A trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie's assassination, does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family.
Robinson has pleaded not guilty to seven charges, including aggravated murder, which can carry the death penalty.
For NPR News, I'm Hugo Rickard Bell in Provo, Utah.
This is NPR. Musician Richard Lloyd has died.
He was a guitarist in the art rock band Television. Lloyd was 75 years old, NPR's Isabella Gomez-Sarmiento reports.
Television grew out of the New York City punk scene in the 1970s, playing at clubs like CBGB.
The interplay between the two guitarists, Richard Lloyd and Tom Berlaine, became a key tenet of the band's improvisational approach to punk.
After releasing two albums, Television disbanded in 1978 and Lloyd went on to pursue solo projects.
But the band and Richard Lloyd's contributions to its kinetic sound are still cited as key innovators in the development of alternative rock,
influencing groups like REM, Caveman and U2. Isabella Gomez-Sarmiento, NPR News.
President Trump says the FBI is investigating NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, but during a White House briefing, Trump said he does not think Huang has anything to worry about.
He called Huang a very honorable man.
NVIDIA shares dropped more than 4 percent Monday after the company announced over the weekend that it's investigating whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
After he acknowledged an extramarital affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy.
Lower oil prices, giving global stock markets a boost.
Some major markets in Europe are rising after stocks into Asia advanced.
South Korean shares closed up more than 4 percent and Japan's benchmark Nikkei rose 2.8 percent.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
Thank you.

Hegseth to hold Pentagon press conference addressing impeachment resolution filed by Thomas Massey
Saudi Arabia's east-west oil pipeline struck, causing fire; second attack after September drone strikes
Trial date set for June 2028 in Tyler Robinson case over Charlie Kirk killing in Utah
Guitarist Richard Lloyd of the band Television dies at age 75
Trump says FBI investigating NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, but says he has nothing to worry about
Global stocks rise on lower oil prices, with South Korean and Japanese shares gaining
